Thought: I need to determine why HFA-134R (a CFC substitute) does not damage the ozone layer. Let me analyze each option:

A. Claims HFA-134R contains hydrogen which can be degraded, preventing ozone damage because not all sites are fluorinated.
B. Claims HFA-134R doesn't contain chlorine, which is the ozone-depleting element.
C. Claims only C compounds deplete ozone.

From my knowledge of chemistry, CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) damage the ozone layer primarily because they contain chlorine atoms that are released in the stratosphere through photodissociation. These chlorine atoms then catalytically destroy ozone molecules. 

HFA-134R (also known as HFC-134a or 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane) is a hydrofluorocarbon that contains hydrogen and fluorine but no chlorine. The absence of chlorine is the key reason it doesn't deplete the ozone layer.

Option B correctly identifies that the absence of chlorine is why HFA-134R doesn't damage the ozone layer.

Option A has some truth (the hydrogen does make it more degradable), but this is not the primary reason.
Option C is incorrect - many carbon compounds don't deplete ozone.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
